obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact-real model distinguished from deterministic f64 evaluation; finite correspondence only
obernants.assumptions: Declared resource cap, finite inputs and successful allocations
obernants.domain: Finite validated f64 API and separately exact-real target
obernants.observation_scope: Return values, errors, rounded arithmetic and named finite assertions
obernants.operator: Within the fixed test transcript universe, pass excludes executions containing any failed assertion; fail excludes executions satisfying all checks under normal completion. Outside the finite schedules no acceptance restriction is established. Panic, allocation and infrastructure failures have distinct causes although all prevent a pass.

obernants.operator: An observed pass has a nonunique preimage: all implementations that satisfy every finite fixture, including implementations wrong elsewhere. A failed named assertion narrows the fiber to executions violating that check but cannot uniquely locate production versus oracle defects. Compiled mutants witness distinct failing implementations.

obernants.operator: Partition enumeration minimizes squared loss without PAVA; support masks solve simplex KKT without sorting; L1 stationarity uses a recovered common multiplier; soft compares subgradients and a separate candidate-objective grid. Each is independent of its production control flow.

obernants.operator: Fixtures cover ties, empty input, zero parameters, nonfinite values and extreme scales. Length caps are directly tested except L1 which delegates tested validation. Allocation refusal is not forced; finite sample success is not universal numerical certification.

obernants.operator: Mutants reverse the PAVA comparison, bias simplex threshold, erase L1 signs, or add soft threshold. Named partition_oracle, active_set_oracle, kkt_grid and subgradient_grid respectively detect them. Positive restoration and source hashes bind observations.
